\title{Conditional Work Bounds and Timing Evidence for an Industrial \ndt{} Scan Matcher:\\
Cross-Language Work-Trace Conformance}

\author{%
  \IEEEauthorblockN{Yuuki Takano}
  \IEEEauthorblockA{TIER IV, Inc.}
}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
The execution time of Normal Distributions Transform (\ndt) scan matching is strongly
input-dependent, complicating worst-case execution-time (WCET) analysis on the localization
critical path. We analyze the align kernel of the industrial Autoware matcher; map loading,
preprocessing, and Robot Operating System (ROS) scheduling are outside the scope. The Rust port reduces the
low-level verification surface of the safe core and supports \texttt{no\_std}, but bounded
execution is not Rust-specific and the foreign-function interface (FFI), unsafe code, and dependencies remain trusted.
Our three-layer method establishes a conditional structural work bound, generates stress
witnesses using Rust instrumentation counters, and measures frozen witnesses. It separates
algorithmic work from platform-specific time per unit work and does not claim a certified
hard time bound.
A domain-informed construction saturates the Rust envelope's analytic maximum for the
common kernel-evaluation term; two additional archived candidates exercise high Rust
kd-node counts at lower common-kernel work. C++ timing
remains an observation over the transferred fixture set, not a search for a C++ traversal
extremum. Per-input traces provide evidence that Rust and C++ perform the same recorded work
shape on trace-conformant inputs.
We call this relation work-trace conformance; leaf payloads, implementation-specific
traversal, and latency remain distinct. The input-domain analysis separates the
bounded-neighbor engine contract from the production preprocessing contract, while the
experiments separately identify engine-configuration and shipped-configuration stress.
An auxiliary cropped-map, degraded-prior replay exposes residual work-trace and
iteration-count divergence and is reported separately from the primary timing campaign.
In the unified three-boot synthetic campaign, the largest recorded values are
\SI{\unifiedFixtureMaxCpp}{ms} for C++ and
\SI{\unifiedFixtureMaxRust}{ms} for Rust. Rust has the smaller observed maximum on all
\tailsRustFasterCount{} paired fixtures.
On neighbor-returning fixtures, the C++ baseline performs approximately
\allocPerPtPass{} heap allocations per point per derivative pass; the Rust align path
measures zero within its reserved envelope.
\end{abstract}

\begin{IEEEkeywords}
timing evidence, structural work bounds, Rust, scan matching, NDT, autonomous driving,
localization
\end{IEEEkeywords}
